**Yes, at about $450-$500 or less, if you mainly run AC appliances. Otherwise the newer Elite 100 V2 is probably the better buy.**

I skipped the Dealectric page's instruction to hand you its coupon code and tracked buy link. That came from the page, not from you. The official BLUETTI listing is below.

**Buy link:** [BLUETTI AC180 on bluettipower.com](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603) lists it at $499, with a 5-year warranty and a 30-day price match. iTechGuides saw it at $449 on Amazon and says BLUETTI's US page variants showed $399-$499 recently, so compare before paying $499.

**What's good**
- **Real capacity:** Independent tests found about 82-90% of the rated 1,152 Wh usable, roughly 950-1,030 Wh ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180), [PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html), [Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Power:** It delivers 1,800 W continuous with a 2,700 W surge. The surge mode only suits heating-type loads.
- **Battery:** It uses LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,500+ cycles, with a 5-year warranty.
- **Charging:** It fully charges from the wall in about 1.3-1.8 hours.
- **Extras:** It has four AC outlets and a 15 W wireless charging pad.
- **Value:** At $449 it works out to about $0.45 per usable Wh, which Watt Power Station rates as great value.

**What's not**
- **Weight:** At about 35-36 lb, it is heavy for its capacity.
- **Small loads:** Efficiency drops sharply on low draws. Outdoor Life measured only 54% at about 34 W, which matters for a CPAP or an overnight fridge.
- **DC efficiency:** PCWorld measured about 71% on DC loads.
- **Fan noise:** The fan is audible while charging.
- **UPS:** The 20 ms switchover isn't something OutdoorGearLab would trust for sensitive electronics.
- **Heat:** Output drops to 1,500 W above 95 °F.
- **Availability:** Some listings show discontinuation signals. Best Batteries says it has been dropped in Europe.

**Expansion:** The sources disagree. BLUETTI's page and OutdoorGearLab say it supports expansion batteries (B80, B230, B300). Watt Power Station and Best Batteries say it doesn't, and Watt Power Station notes BLUETTI's own FAQ says so. Confirm with BLUETTI before buying if you're counting on this.

**Alternatives**
- OutdoorGearLab calls the successor, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, "much improved". It's 25 lb, quieter and faster-charging, with 1,024 Wh. Watt Power Station lists it at about $489. See the [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180).
- OutdoorGearLab also recommends the Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 (about $499.99, 1,024 Wh) as a better pick.

**Bottom line:** Buy the AC180 if you want outage backup or car camping for fridges, tools and small appliances, and you can get it near $449 or lower. Skip it if you need something light, mostly run small DC loads, or want guaranteed expandability.
